Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. majorRoadLengthKmWithin1600m.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. averageSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Current window 2025-04-03 to 2026-04-03; prior window 2024-04-02 to 2025-04-02 for trend proxy. Sample transactions=5, postcodes with transactions=4, strata={'inner': 0, 'middle': 3, 'outer': 2, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 0, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

averageSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Current window 2025-04-03 to 2026-04-03; prior window 2024-04-02 to 2025-04-02 for trend proxy. Sample transactions=6, postcodes with transactions=5, strata={'inner': 2, 'middle': 2, 'outer': 2, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 0, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

averageSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Current window 2025-04-03 to 2026-04-03; prior window 2024-04-02 to 2025-04-02 for trend proxy. Sample transactions=6, postcodes with transactions=3, strata={'inner': 0, 'middle': 0, 'outer': 6, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 0, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Main roads are motorway, trunk, primary, and secondary classes plus their link roads. The stored metrics are nearest distance from the station centroid to the nearest mapped main road and total main-road length intersecting a 1600m station buffer (2x the default 800m catchment). Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

majorRoadLengthKmWithin1600m.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. Counts are averaged into an annualised per-1,000 rate using the station 1800m catchment population denominator when available, otherwise the nearest-anchor population fallback.

averageSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Current window 2025-04-03 to 2026-04-03; prior window 2024-04-02 to 2025-04-02 for trend proxy. Sample transactions=4, postcodes with transactions=4, strata={'inner': 2, 'middle': 2, 'outer': 0, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 0, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. The stored metrics are nearest distance from the station centroid to the nearest mapped main road and total main-road length intersecting a 1600m station buffer (2x the default 800m catchment). Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. Counts are averaged into an annualised per-1,000 rate using the station 1800m catchment population denominator when available, otherwise the nearest-anchor population fallback.

nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

averageSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Current window 2025-04-03 to 2026-04-03; prior window 2024-04-02 to 2025-04-02 for trend proxy. Sample transactions=9, postcodes with transactions=7, strata={'inner': 5, 'middle': 4, 'outer': 0, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 0, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

averageSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. averageSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Current window 2025-04-03 to 2026-04-03; prior window 2024-04-02 to 2025-04-02 for trend proxy. Sample transactions=18, postcodes with transactions=11, strata={'inner': 4, 'middle': 12, 'outer': 2, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 0, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

averageSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Current window 2025-04-03 to 2026-04-03; prior window 2024-04-02 to 2025-04-02 for trend proxy. Sample transactions=22, postcodes with transactions=16, strata={'inner': 10, 'middle': 10, 'outer': 2, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 0, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Current window 2025-04-03 to 2026-04-03; prior window 2024-04-02 to 2025-04-02 for trend proxy. Sample transactions=6, postcodes with transactions=6, strata={'inner': 1, 'middle': 5, 'outer': 0, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 0, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

greenSpaceAreaKm2Within1km.methodologyNote: Direct greenspace geometry calculation from Ordnance Survey OS Open Greenspace. Area is measured as intersecting greenspace within a 1km station buffer, green cover is measured within a wider 1600m buffer (2x the default 800m catchment radius), and nearest park distance uses the nearest mapped public access point where available, otherwise the nearest greenspace boundary.

nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Main roads are motorway, trunk, primary, and secondary classes plus their link roads. The stored metrics are nearest distance from the station centroid to the nearest mapped main road and total main-road length intersecting a 1600m station buffer (2x the default 800m catchment). Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

majorRoadLengthKmWithin1600m.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. Counts are averaged into an annualised per-1,000 rate using the station 1800m catchment population denominator when available, otherwise the nearest-anchor population fallback.

Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

secondaryQualityScore.methodologyNote: Secondary phase is intentionally excluded from the current school ranking model.

annualPm25.methodologyNote: DEFRA UK-AIR modelled background pollution data (2024); station-centred 800m catchment value from distance-weighted 1km grid cells.

greenSpaceAreaKm2Within1km.methodologyNote: Direct greenspace geometry calculation from Ordnance Survey OS Open Greenspace. Area is measured as intersecting greenspace within a 1km station buffer, green cover is measured within a wider 1600m buffer (2x the default 800m catchment radius), and nearest park distance uses the nearest mapped public access point where available, otherwise the nearest greenspace boundary.

greenCoverPct.methodologyNote: Direct greenspace geometry calculation from Ordnance Survey OS Open Greenspace. nearestParkDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct greenspace geometry calculation from Ordnance Survey OS Open Greenspace. nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Main roads are motorway, trunk, primary, and secondary classes plus their link roads. The stored metrics are nearest distance from the station centroid to the nearest mapped main road and total main-road length intersecting a 1600m station buffer (2x the default 800m catchment). Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

majorRoadLengthKmWithin1600m.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. Counts are averaged into an annualised per-1,000 rate using the station 1800m catchment population denominator when available, otherwise the nearest-anchor population fallback.

nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

greenSpaceAreaKm2Within1km.methodologyNote: Direct greenspace geometry calculation from Ordnance Survey OS Open Greenspace. Area is measured as intersecting greenspace within a 1km station buffer, green cover is measured within a wider 1600m buffer (2x the default 800m catchment radius), and nearest park distance uses the nearest mapped public access point where available, otherwise the nearest greenspace boundary.

greenCoverPct.methodologyNote: Direct greenspace geometry calculation from Ordnance Survey OS Open Greenspace. nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Main roads are motorway, trunk, primary, and secondary classes plus their link roads. The stored metrics are nearest distance from the station centroid to the nearest mapped main road and total main-road length intersecting a 1600m station buffer (2x the default 800m catchment). Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

majorRoadLengthKmWithin1600m.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. Counts are averaged into an annualised per-1,000 rate using the station 1800m catchment population denominator when available, otherwise the nearest-anchor population fallback.

boroughQolScore.methodologyNote: Derived from ONS APS personal well-being means for the latest period (life satisfaction, worthwhile, happiness, and inverted anxiety), aggregated to a positive well-being composite.

Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

averageSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Current window 2025-04-03 to 2026-04-03; prior window 2024-04-02 to 2025-04-02 for trend proxy. Sample transactions=3, postcodes with transactions=3, strata={'inner': 2, 'middle': 1, 'outer': 0, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 0, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. averageSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Current window 2025-04-03 to 2026-04-03; prior window 2024-04-02 to 2025-04-02 for trend proxy. Sample transactions=4, postcodes with transactions=3, strata={'inner': 2, 'middle': 2, 'outer': 0, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 0, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

averageSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Current window 2025-04-03 to 2026-04-03; prior window 2024-04-02 to 2025-04-02 for trend proxy. Sample transactions=7, postcodes with transactions=7, strata={'inner': 0, 'middle': 1, 'outer': 6, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 0, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

nearestParkDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct greenspace geometry calculation from Ordnance Survey OS Open Greenspace. nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Main roads are motorway, trunk, primary, and secondary classes plus their link roads. The stored metrics are nearest distance from the station centroid to the nearest mapped main road and total main-road length intersecting a 1600m station buffer (2x the default 800m catchment). Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

averageSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Sample transactions=5, postcodes with transactions=4, strata={'inner': 1, 'middle': 4, 'outer': 0, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 0, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. majorRoadLengthKmWithin1600m.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Main roads are motorway, trunk, primary, and secondary classes plus their link roads. The stored metrics are nearest distance from the station centroid to the nearest mapped main road and total main-road length intersecting a 1600m station buffer (2x the default 800m catchment). majorRoadLengthKmWithin1600m.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. Counts are averaged into an annualised per-1,000 rate using the station 1800m catchment population denominator when available, otherwise the nearest-anchor population fallback.

averageSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Current window 2025-04-03 to 2026-04-03; prior window 2024-04-02 to 2025-04-02 for trend proxy. Sample transactions=3, postcodes with transactions=2, strata={'inner': 0, 'middle': 3, 'outer': 0, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 0, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Main roads are motorway, trunk, primary, and secondary classes plus their link roads. The stored metrics are nearest distance from the station centroid to the nearest mapped main road and total main-road length intersecting a 1600m station buffer (2x the default 800m catchment). Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

majorRoadLengthKmWithin1600m.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. Counts are averaged into an annualised per-1,000 rate using the station 1800m catchment population denominator when available, otherwise the nearest-anchor population fallback.

Sample transactions=5, postcodes with transactions=5, strata={'inner': 2, 'middle': 3, 'outer': 0, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 0, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

greenCoverPct.methodologyNote: Direct greenspace geometry calculation from Ordnance Survey OS Open Greenspace. nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Main roads are motorway, trunk, primary, and secondary classes plus their link roads. The stored metrics are nearest distance from the station centroid to the nearest mapped main road and total main-road length intersecting a 1600m station buffer (2x the default 800m catchment). Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

majorRoadLengthKmWithin1600m.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. Counts are averaged into an annualised per-1,000 rate using the station 1800m catchment population denominator when available, otherwise the nearest-anchor population fallback.

boroughQolScore.methodologyNote: Derived from ONS APS personal well-being means for the latest period (life satisfaction, worthwhile, happiness, and inverted anxiety), aggregated to a positive well-being composite.

averageSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 1600m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Current window 2025-04-03 to 2026-04-03; prior window 2024-04-02 to 2025-04-02 for trend proxy. Sample transactions=5, postcodes with transactions=5, strata={'inner': 0, 'middle': 0, 'outer': 0, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 5, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. The stored metrics are nearest distance from the station centroid to the nearest mapped main road and total main-road length intersecting a 1600m station buffer (2x the default 800m catchment). Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

majorRoadLengthKmWithin1600m.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. Counts are averaged into an annualised per-1,000 rate using the station 1800m catchment population denominator when available, otherwise the nearest-anchor population fallback.

nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

greenSpaceAreaKm2Within1km.methodologyNote: Direct greenspace geometry calculation from Ordnance Survey OS Open Greenspace. Area is measured as intersecting greenspace within a 1km station buffer, green cover is measured within a wider 1600m buffer (2x the default 800m catchment radius), and nearest park distance uses the nearest mapped public access point where available, otherwise the nearest greenspace boundary.

greenCoverPct.methodologyNote: Direct greenspace geometry calculation from Ordnance Survey OS Open Greenspace. Area is measured as intersecting greenspace within a 1km station buffer, green cover is measured within a wider 1600m buffer (2x the default 800m catchment radius), and nearest park distance uses the nearest mapped public access point where available, otherwise the nearest greenspace boundary.

nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Main roads are motorway, trunk, primary, and secondary classes plus their link roads. The stored metrics are nearest distance from the station centroid to the nearest mapped main road and total main-road length intersecting a 1600m station buffer (2x the default 800m catchment). Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

majorRoadLengthKmWithin1600m.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Main roads are motorway, trunk, primary, and secondary classes plus their link roads. Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. Counts are averaged into an annualised per-1,000 rate using the station 1800m catchment population denominator when available, otherwise the nearest-anchor population fallback.

boroughQolScore.methodologyNote: Derived from ONS APS personal well-being means for the latest period (life satisfaction, worthwhile, happiness, and inverted anxiety), aggregated to a positive well-being composite.

nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

averageSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Current window 2025-04-03 to 2026-04-03; prior window 2024-04-02 to 2025-04-02 for trend proxy. Sample transactions=4, postcodes with transactions=4, strata={'inner': 2, 'middle': 1, 'outer': 1, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 0, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

medianSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Current window 2025-04-03 to 2026-04-03; prior window 2024-04-02 to 2025-04-02 for trend proxy. nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

greenCoverPct.methodologyNote: Direct greenspace geometry calculation from Ordnance Survey OS Open Greenspace. nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Main roads are motorway, trunk, primary, and secondary classes plus their link roads. The stored metrics are nearest distance from the station centroid to the nearest mapped main road and total main-road length intersecting a 1600m station buffer (2x the default 800m catchment). Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

majorRoadLengthKmWithin1600m.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. Counts are averaged into an annualised per-1,000 rate using the station 1800m catchment population denominator when available, otherwise the nearest-anchor population fallback.

boroughQolScore.methodologyNote: Derived from ONS APS personal well-being means for the latest period (life satisfaction, worthwhile, happiness, and inverted anxiety), aggregated to a positive well-being composite.

nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Main roads are motorway, trunk, primary, and secondary classes plus their link roads. The stored metrics are nearest distance from the station centroid to the nearest mapped main road and total main-road length intersecting a 1600m station buffer (2x the default 800m catchment). majorRoadLengthKmWithin1600m.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. Counts are averaged into an annualised per-1,000 rate using the station 1800m catchment population denominator when available, otherwise the nearest-anchor population fallback.

Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

averageSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Current window 2025-04-03 to 2026-04-03; prior window 2024-04-02 to 2025-04-02 for trend proxy. Sample transactions=18, postcodes with transactions=15, strata={'inner': 0, 'middle': 10, 'outer': 8, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 0, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

greenSpaceAreaKm2Within1km.methodologyNote: Direct greenspace geometry calculation from Ordnance Survey OS Open Greenspace. Area is measured as intersecting greenspace within a 1km station buffer, green cover is measured within a wider 1600m buffer (2x the default 800m catchment radius), and nearest park distance uses the nearest mapped public access point where available, otherwise the nearest greenspace boundary.

greenCoverPct.methodologyNote: Direct greenspace geometry calculation from Ordnance Survey OS Open Greenspace. nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Main roads are motorway, trunk, primary, and secondary classes plus their link roads. The stored metrics are nearest distance from the station centroid to the nearest mapped main road and total main-road length intersecting a 1600m station buffer (2x the default 800m catchment). Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

majorRoadLengthKmWithin1600m.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. Counts are averaged into an annualised per-1,000 rate using the station 1800m catchment population denominator when available, otherwise the nearest-anchor population fallback.

Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

annualPm25.methodologyNote: DEFRA UK-AIR modelled background pollution data (2024); station-centred 800m catchment value from distance-weighted 1km grid cells.

greenSpaceAreaKm2Within1km.methodologyNote: Direct greenspace geometry calculation from Ordnance Survey OS Open Greenspace. greenCoverPct.methodologyNote: Direct greenspace geometry calculation from Ordnance Survey OS Open Greenspace. nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Main roads are motorway, trunk, primary, and secondary classes plus their link roads. The stored metrics are nearest distance from the station centroid to the nearest mapped main road and total main-road length intersecting a 1600m station buffer (2x the default 800m catchment). Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

majorRoadLengthKmWithin1600m.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. crimeRatePerThousand.methodologyNote: Direct monthly street-level crime archive aggregation from data.police.uk for all currently available months since 2023-01 within an 1800m station radius, using the official archive download for BTP, City of London, Metropolitan, and London-boundary forces. Counts are averaged into an annualised per-1,000 rate using the station 1800m catchment population denominator when available, otherwise the nearest-anchor population fallback.

boroughQolScore.methodologyNote: Derived from ONS APS personal well-being means for the latest period (life satisfaction, worthwhile, happiness, and inverted anxiety), aggregated to a positive well-being composite.

averageSemiDetachedPrice.methodologyNote: Fallback property metric when current 3-bed / 2-bath asking-price coverage is too thin. HM Land Registry PPD semi-detached standard transactions. Catchment postcode sample from postcodes.io within 800m using capped distance bands with lower weights for outer rings. Median/average are distance-and-recency weighted so nearer catchment transactions and newer sales have higher influence (band weights taper from the inner catchment into the outer fallback rings). Current window 2025-04-03 to 2026-04-03; prior window 2024-04-02 to 2025-04-02 for trend proxy. Sample transactions=6, postcodes with transactions=6, strata={'inner': 2, 'middle': 2, 'outer': 2, 'extended_inner': 0, 'extended_outer': 0, 'far_inner': 0, 'far_middle': 0, 'far_outer': 0}.

nearbyPrimaryCount.methodologyNote: The current school model is primary-only and uses state-funded-only official sources. Counts come from open state-funded GIAS establishment exports, excluding private schools. Reachable-primary access still starts from an approximate 20-minute road-adjusted drive proxy, but schools are now downweighted when open admissions are less likely in practice: distance matters most, faith-designated schools are discounted, larger schools get a modest capacity uplift, schools that already look very full relative to their published capacity are penalised, and all-through schools get a small penalty. National open data does not directly expose sibling or feeder priorities or school-level cut-off distances, so this remains a cautious admissions-reachability heuristic rather than a true offer-probability model. Primary quality now uses the latest eligible 2023-onward KS2 attainment basket from 202324-202425 (combined expected standard, combined higher standard, average reading scaled score, average maths scaled score). Attendance is a separate light-touch supplement from 202324 official primary absence data (overall absence and persistent absence). Ofsted is not the main driver: latest published inspection outcomes as at 2025-08-31 are used only as a warning overlay and modest penalty for weaker leadership, behaviour, safeguarding, or overall effectiveness.

nearestMainRoadDistanceM.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass. Main roads are motorway, trunk, primary, and secondary classes plus their link roads. The stored metrics are nearest distance from the station centroid to the nearest mapped main road and total main-road length intersecting a 1600m station buffer (2x the default 800m catchment). Farther nearest distance and less intersecting main-road length are treated as better in the ranking.

majorRoadLengthKmWithin1600m.methodologyNote: Direct major-road exposure metrics from current OpenStreetMap highway geometry via Overpass.
